summary: Yellow-brick light on Lake Superior's Keweenaw shore, lit in 1919 to replace the Eagle River light; automated 1939, dark 1954, now private and closed.

facts.agency: Privately owned; Bud Cole since 2019 (LighthouseFriends names him Edward Cole)

events.note: W. C. Moreland aground on Eagle River (Sawtooth) Reef on 18 October 1910 in smoke from a forest fire
Gas and bell buoy placed on the reef on 10 June 1916; taken away when the temporary light was set up in 1917
Temporary light and electric siren established 14 September 1917; station renamed Sand Hills Light Station in August 1917
Congress appropriates $70,000 by the act of 12 June 1917
Fog signal placed in operation 15 May 1919
Main light first shown 19 June 1919 (Commissioner); Terry Pepper gives 18 June
Coast Guard automates the light with an acetylene lamp; keepers withdrawn
Coast Guard assumes responsibility for the aids to navigation
Temporarily reopened as a wartime Coast Guard training facility; closed again in 1943
Sold 1958 to H. Donald Bliss (public auction per Terry Pepper; sealed bids per LighthouseFriends)
Bought by Bill Frabotta, who converted the fog-signal building into a summer cottage
Sand Hills Lighthouse Inn opens as a bed-and-breakfast after a 1992-1995 renovation
Bud Cole buys the station (LighthouseFriends: Edward Cole); the Society's 2022 item also gives 2014 for a Cole purchase of the property; the property is closed for a multi-year restoration

corrections.why: The USLHS record gives the tower shape as SQUARE, and LighthouseFriends describes a square tower. The station record says conical.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A temporary light and electric siren were established at Sand Hills on 14 September 1917 (LighthouseFriends), which explains the 1917 date some sources give. The permanent light was first shown in June 1919 (Commissioner's report, Terry Pepper).

Terry Pepper says William R. Bennetts was sole head keeper through all the manned years and exhibited the light on 18 June 1919; the archive lists De Champlain as principal keeper 1917-1919 and LighthouseFriends says De Champlain died in June 1919 and Bennetts came in September 1919. The story states the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Thin-to-moderate station. No NRHP nomination: NPGallery 94000746 is an undigitised placeholder and the NARA catalog is off limits, so the 1994 NRHP listing is in the record but not used. The USCG Historian's Sand Hills page could not be read (archive.org copies returned only the Wayback calendar). Wikipedia was read for leads only. Conflicts left in the text: distance from Eagle River (12 miles per the Board and Terry Pepper, about 4 miles per the 1915 Commissioner estimate); first lighting (19 June per the Commissioner and LighthouseFriends, 18 June per Terry Pepper); temporary light (September 1917 per LighthouseFriends, spring 1918 per Terry Pepper, 'in commission' per the 1919 Bulletin); tower (square and 91 ft to the lantern per USLHS, 70 ft per LighthouseFriends; the station record says conical). The De Champlain spelling varies (De Champlain, DeChamplain). Roster stints are the USLHS archive's own (NARA registers via the Kraig Anderson inventory) and were not checked against the registers; the keepers' post-1939 names are not in the prose. The Bulletin and Commissioner page numbers are from the corpus OCR index: printed page numbers are as read; the LHB 1891-92 citation gives the scan page only. Terry Pepper and LighthouseFriends are private history sites, used for facts with short paraphrase. The research date is 2026-10-27 (the system date when the WLOX Biloxi article was read), not 2026-10-22 as the batch note says. Fact-check additions (2026-10-22 check): LighthouseFriends says a fifth-order Fresnel lens, never used at Sand Hills, is on display in the tower; the record and the Commissioner give the fourth-order lens, which the story uses. The Commissioner's 1919 description gives buff-colored pressed brick (scan p. 485); Terry Pepper and the Society's record say yellow brick. The Commissioner's FY1919 report is cited at printed p. 49 (18 June, about three miles, $68,714.69) and p. 87 (19 June); both are read from the OCR page index and the p. 49 and 87 numbers were confirmed by corpus.py page. The archive's roster matches the 14 stints in the story (2 principal, 7 first, 5 second assistants). Bud Cole is named in the Society's 2022 item; LighthouseFriends calls the same 2019 buyer Edward Cole. The Society's 2014 purchase date conflicts with its own 2019 date and is stated in the story.
